title: Sections of a quasi-coherent module on nested affine opens satisfy tensor base change
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $\mathcal M$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module. For affine opens $U\subseteq U'$ of $S$, put $R=\mathcal O_S(U)$, $R'=\mathcal O_S(U')$, $M=\mathcal M(U)$ and $M'=\mathcal M(U')$. Then the canonical $R$-linear map $M'\otimes_{R'}R\to M$, $m'\otimes r\mapsto r\,m'|_U$, is an isomorphism.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01LN (lemma-spec-inclusion), using Schemes Lemmas 01I9 and 01IA

proof.text: *The affine charts.* Let $\iota_U:\operatorname{Spec}R\to S$ and $\iota_{U'}:\operatorname{Spec}R'\to S$ be the canonical open immersions with images $U$ and $U'$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points], and $\rho:R'\to R$ the restriction map. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-inclusion-spec-map], $j:=\operatorname{Spec}\rho:\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$ is an open immersion and $\iota_{U'}\circ j=\iota_U$; this is the bottom arrow $U\to U'$ of the square of Constructions 01LN, a morphism of affine schemes given by the ring map $\rho$.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01LN (lemma-spec-inclusion), proof, first sentence ('the map $R\otimes_{R'}A'\to A$ is an isomorphism as $\mathcal A$ is quasi-coherent (see Schemes, Lemma 01I9)'); Schemes, Lemma 01I2 (morphisms of affine schemes are Spec of ring maps)

proof.text: *$\mathcal M$ on $U'$ is $\widetilde{M'}$.* Put $\mathcal N'=\mathcal M|_{\operatorname{Spec}R'}$, the restriction of $\mathcal M$ along the open immersion $\iota_{U'}$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]: $\mathcal N'(V)=\mathcal M(\iota_{U'}(V))$, so $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R',\mathcal N')=\mathcal M(U')=M'$, and $R'=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R',\mathcal O)$ acts on it through $\iota_{U'}^\sharp:\mathcal O_S(U')\cong R'$, i.e. by the given $R'$-module structure of $M'$. By part (2) of that node $\mathcal N'$ is quasi-coherent, so by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3) the counit $\varepsilon:\widetilde{M'}\to\mathcal N'$, the map of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R'}$-modules corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_{M'}$, is an isomorphism; by the description of the adjunction bijection in (1), $\varepsilon_{\operatorname{Spec}R'}(\tau(m'))=m'$ for $m'\in M'$.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01LN (lemma-spec-inclusion), proof, first sentence ('the map $R\otimes_{R'}A'\to A$ is an isomorphism as $\mathcal A$ is quasi-coherent (see Schemes, Lemma 01I9)'); Schemes, Lemmas 01IA (lemma-quasi-coherent-affine) and 01IB (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent): a quasi-coherent module on Spec R' is the sheaf associated to its global sections

proof.text: *Restricting to $U$.* Restrict $\mathcal N'$ along $j$: $(\mathcal N'|_{\operatorname{Spec}R})(V)=\mathcal N'(j(V))=\mathcal M(\iota_{U'}(j(V)))=\mathcal M(\iota_U(V))$, with the same restriction maps and the same $\mathcal O$-action (both through $\iota_U^\sharp$, since $\iota_{U'}\circ j=\iota_U$), so $\mathcal N'|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$ is the restriction of $\mathcal M$ along $\iota_U$ and $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal N'|_{\operatorname{Spec}R})=\mathcal N'(j(\operatorname{Spec}R))=\mathcal M(U)=M$, the $R$-module structure being the given one. For $m'\in M'=\mathcal N'(\operatorname{Spec}R')$ the element $m'|_{j(\operatorname{Spec}R)}$ of this module is $m'|_U$.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01LN (lemma-spec-inclusion), proof, first sentence ('the map $R\otimes_{R'}A'\to A$ is an isomorphism as $\mathcal A$ is quasi-coherent (see Schemes, Lemma 01I9)'); the identification of the square's bottom arrow with $U\subseteq U'$

proof.text:
*The pullback of $\widetilde{M'}$.* Apply the restriction functor along $j$ to the isomorphism $\varepsilon$ of step 2 and combine with [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction] and [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change] (for $\varphi=\rho$, $\psi=j$): this gives isomorphisms of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$-modules
$$\widetilde{R\otimes_{R'}M'}\xrightarrow{\theta^{-1}}j^*\widetilde{M'}\xrightarrow{\kappa^{-1}}\widetilde{M'}|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\xrightarrow{\varepsilon|}\mathcal N'|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}.$$
Taking sections over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and precomposing with the isomorphism $\tau:R\otimes_{R'}M'\to\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\widetilde{R\otimes_{R'}M'})$ of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (2), and using step 3, gives a bijection $\Phi:R\otimes_{R'}M'\to M$. It is $R$-linear: each map in the chain is a morphism of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$-modules, hence linear over $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal O)=R$ on global sections, and $\tau$ is $R$-linear.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01LN (lemma-spec-inclusion), proof, first sentence ('the map $R\otimes_{R'}A'\to A$ is an isomorphism as $\mathcal A$ is quasi-coherent (see Schemes, Lemma 01I9)'); Schemes, Lemma 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback) (1): $\psi^*\widetilde M=\widetilde{S\otimes_RM}$, applied to $\psi=j$; for an open immersion the pullback of modules is the restriction (Sheaves, Lemma 00A0)

proof.text: *$\Phi$ is the canonical map.* Let $m'\in M'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change], $\theta^{-1}(\tau(1\otimes m'))=\eta(\tau(m'))$, the image of $\tau(m')\in\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R',\widetilde{M'})$ under the unit of $j^*\dashv j_*$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction] (with $W=\operatorname{Spec}R'$, $f^{-1}W=\operatorname{Spec}R$), $\kappa^{-1}(\eta(\tau(m')))=\tau(m')|_{j(\operatorname{Spec}R)}$. Since $\varepsilon$ is a morphism of sheaves it commutes with restriction, so $\varepsilon(\tau(m')|_{j(\operatorname{Spec}R)})=\varepsilon_{\operatorname{Spec}R'}(\tau(m'))|_{j(\operatorname{Spec}R)}=m'|_U$ by steps 2 and 3. Hence $\Phi(1\otimes m')=m'|_U$, and by $R$-linearity $\Phi(r\otimes m')=r\,m'|_U$. So $\Phi$ is the canonical map $M'\otimes_{R'}R\cong R\otimes_{R'}M'\to M$ of the statement, which is therefore an isomorphism.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01LN (lemma-spec-inclusion), proof, first sentence ('the map $R\otimes_{R'}A'\to A$ is an isomorphism as $\mathcal A$ is quasi-coherent (see Schemes, Lemma 01I9)'); the isomorphism there is 'the map $R\otimes_{R'}A'\to A$', i.e. the canonical map; this check is not written in the source and is written out here
